column15: Distillery is in Bushmills, County Antrim, Northern Ireland (UK, not the Republic of Ireland) -- GB used since no GB-NIR code exists in the closed list. Range spans single malt (10/12/16/21yo) and blended (Original, Black Bush, Red Bush) so defaultTypeName left empty. Irish whiskey wiki page: peat is rarely used outside Scotland, no exception listed for Bushmills. Country normalized GB -> IE: the closed list has no GB-NIR and this seed follows the Irish-whiskey GI convention.
Official site: "To craft our distinct unpeated whisky...every bottle of Bunnahabhain". Peated range is the sibling Moine (see rule row), matching BRIEF.md's own documented Bunnahabhain/Moine pair.

Fingerprint malts (Miltonduff, Glenburgie) are unpeated Speyside distilleries; wiki page describes the 21 Year Old as "spicy, aromatic and heather smoke", implying a light smoky character at least in aged expressions. Core Finest not separately described in the source, so confidence kept low rather than assuming it is identical to the 21yo.

Wiki: "one of the lighter Islay whiskies, pale in colour, with peaty, floral and peppery notes"; ~95% of production goes into Johnnie Walker Black. Classified medium (not heavy) given the explicit "lighter" framing relative to Ardbeg/Lagavulin-style heavy Islay malts. See rule row for the distillery's occasional unpeated release.
Kentucky straight bourbon whiskey, Lawrenceburg KY, owned by Kirin (Japan) since 2002. Bourbon is not a peated category.

No Wikipedia page found and retailer sites (Master of Malt etc.) return 403; owner/producer could not be verified this session. Treated as an ordinary own-label blended Scotch per default rule -- peat category citation is the general Scotch whisky article (peating is a distillery/product-specific choice, not universal).

Canonical peated sibling of unpeated Tobermory (same distillery, historically the distillery's own original name). Wiki: "The Tobermory Single Malt is distilled from unpeated malted barley...A heavily peated whisky is also produced...named Ledaig." This is the exact defect pattern named in BRIEF.md.

Mainland west-coast Argyll town, not one of the market-convention "islands" -- region=highland matches the authority TSV. Wiki: whisky described as "West Highland" flavour "falling between the dry, smoky style of the...islands and the lighter, sweeter malts of the Highlands", i.e. lightly smoky.

Flagship Heaven Hill bourbon brand (wiki: "its flagship bourbon labels, Evan Williams and Elijah Craig"). defaultTypeName left empty because the catalogue's own samples include flavoured liqueur SKUs (Fire, Honey, Cherry) alongside straight bourbon (1783, Black, Bottled in Bond) -- range spans types. Bourbon base spirit is unpeated.

Blended Canadian whisky, produced at the former Hiram Walker distillery (Windsor, Ontario); owned by Suntory Global Spirits (formerly Beam Suntory) since 2011, part of the Jim Beam portfolio. No Canadian-Club-specific peat statement found; peat citation is the general "peat is rarely used in the malting process outside of Scotland" statement on the Irish whiskey page, used here as a category-level source for a non-Scotch whisky.

Catalogue brand string is "Maison Des Futailles Spicebox" (aliased verbatim). Canadian spiced/flavoured whisky line (Pumpkin, Chocolat, Cinnamon, Ginger Bread, Canadian Spiced). No dedicated citation found for the brand itself; peat citation is the general non-Scotch-unpeated statement (see canadian-club note). defaultTypeName left empty -- flavoured/spiced products, not a standard category.

Region/owner confirmed via the local authority TSV (Speyside, Diageo, malt, operating) and corroborated by its own Wikipedia article, but no source opened this session states its peat level explicitly; a Speyside regional generalisation was considered but the Scotch whisky wiki page itself quotes a source claiming Speyside malts show "smokiness", so region alone was not treated as a safe stand-in. Left peatProfile unknown rather than guess.
No web presence found (own-label, no Wikipedia page, retailer sites blocked). Treated as an ordinary blended Scotch per the own-label default; see glen-talloch note for the peat citation rationale.

Catalogue spells it "BAGOTS" (Grain Game, Madeira Cask, Triple Batch, White Moscatel Cask -- cask-finish naming typical of small-batch/craft bottlings). No Wikipedia page or other citable source found; country and category could not be determined this session.

J&B Rare Scotch whisky, produced by Justerini & Brooks (owned by Diageo); wiki confirms it is a blend of 42 malt and grain whiskies with named fingerprint malts Knockando, Auchroisk, Strathmill and Glen Spey (all unpeated Speyside distilleries), but the article makes no statement about peat/smoke level for the blend itself, so peatProfile is left unknown rather than assumed from the unpeated fingerprint malts alone.

Independent craft distillery in Newport, Kentucky, confirmed real via the Kentucky Bourbon Trail wiki page ("Northern Craft Tour: New Riff Distillery in Newport"). Produces both bourbon and rye (samples: Malted Rye, Bottled in Bond, Bottled-in-Bond Rye) so defaultTypeName left empty. Bourbon/rye are not peated categories.

No web presence found for this own-label (Honey-flavoured variant present in samples). Treated as an ordinary blended Scotch per the own-label default; see glen-talloch note for the peat citation rationale.

Blended Canadian whisky created by Seagram, owned by Diageo since 2000; blended/bottled in Amherstburg, Ontario. No Crown-Royal-specific peat statement found; peat citation is the general non-Scotch-unpeated statement (see canadian-club note).

Rothes, Speyside; owned by Diageo; nearly its entire production goes into J&B blends (own Wikipedia article confirms region/owner/founding 1878). No source opened this session states its own peat level; left unknown rather than assume from the general Speyside association (see benrinnes note on why a bare regional generalisation was not used).

Believed to be associated with the Wemyss family (name matches the Earl of Wemyss's courtesy title, and the family runs Wemyss Malts/Kingsbarns distillery), but no citation could be opened this session confirming producer or peat level -- Wikipedia has no article and other searches returned nothing relevant. bottlerSlug intentionally left empty pending verification (contrast peat-chimney/spice-king, where the Wemyss link is well-established general knowledge).

Catalogue samples (Cigar Series, Cask Strength, Madeira Cask Strength) suggest a small craft/private rye-style label. No Wikipedia page or other citable source found this session; country and category undetermined.

Samples (Yuzu, Classic, Passion Fruit) read as a flavoured whisky-based drink rather than a conventional Scotch/Japanese whisky; zero Wikipedia search hits. Likely a fantasy/evocative brand name for the Eastern European market rather than an actual Japanese producer -- left fully unknown rather than assume Japan from the name alone.

Bud Spencer (samples: The Legend, The Legend Mini) most likely trades on the name of the Italian actor Carlo Pedersoli (stage name Bud Spencer) as licensed merchandise; Wikipedia search only returns his biography, no dedicated drinks-brand page. Could not confirm whether the liquid is actually whisky (celebrity-branded rum is at least as plausible) -- flagging for reviewer attention rather than guessing kind/country/peat.
Straight bourbon brand of Buffalo Trace Distillery (wiki: "Eagle Rare -- straight bourbon and 17 year antique collection"), owned by the Sazerac Company. Bourbon is not a peated category.
No web presence found (own-label, no Wikipedia page). Treated as an ordinary blended Scotch per the own-label default; see glen-talloch note for the peat citation rationale.

Country inferred from the sample product names themselves ("Corn" is a defined American whiskey category; "Northwest" matches the historical Lewis and Clark expedition's Pacific Northwest route) rather than from a citation naming this specific brand -- no Wikipedia page or other source found. Peat citation is the general non-Scotch-unpeated statement (see canadian-club note). defaultTypeName left empty (Corn vs. an unspecified Northwest expression may differ in category).

O.H. Ingram River Aged/"...Flagship" -- initials-plus-surname is a common American whiskey brand-naming convention (cf. E.H. Taylor, W.L. Weller), so US is a low-confidence inference from the name alone; no citation confirms the specific producer. Peat citation is the general non-Scotch-unpeated statement (see canadian-club note).
Generic own-label name, no web presence found. Treated as an ordinary blended Scotch per the own-label default; see glen-talloch note for the peat citation rationale.

Samples ("Rhino's Pastoral", "Old Rhino Rye Spirit") -- the "Spirit" wording may mean this does not even meet whisky's minimum-aging definition (an EU "spirit drink" rather than whisky). No web presence found; country/category undetermined, flagging for reviewer attention.

Sample "Alchemist Tobermory" reads as an independent bottler's expression of Tobermory single malt; no citation confirms which "Alchemist" company this is (several drinks businesses use the name). countryCode GB-SCT is a low-confidence inference from bottling a Scotch distillery, not a confirmed fact. A tobermory distillery row is emitted below (required per BRIEF.md sec.2 regardless of this bottler's own identity) so the in-name distillery match can resolve.

Single generic product line with no other qualifier; "Boulevardier" is otherwise a classic bourbon/Campari/vermouth cocktail name, so this may be a bottled RTD cocktail mis-filed under whisky rather than an actual whiskey brand (same concern as Ice Drive, see final report) rather than a whiskey brand -- left fully unknown.

Craft distillery, Spokane, Washington -- confirmed real via the American Distilling Institute wiki page (2010/2011 Bubble Cap "Distillery of the Year"). Known for wheat whiskey (not one of the 8 listed defaultTypeName values, left empty). American whiskey categories are not peated.
No web presence found (own-label). Treated as an ordinary blended Scotch per the own-label default; see glen-talloch note for the peat citation rationale.
Single product, just "Kyoda". Wikipedia search returns nothing relevant (only an unrelated anime director's surname). No basis found for country, category or peat.

Catalogue spells it "Mckintrye's Club & Casino" (aliased verbatim); name corrected here to the likelier intended spelling "McKintyre's". No web presence found; treated as an ordinary blended Scotch own-label per default rule -- see glen-talloch note for the peat citation rationale.

Tomintoul distillery's peated single malt, released under its old spring-name "Ballantruan" rather than the Tomintoul brand name. Wiki: "a 1991 peaty vintage was released under the name 'Old Ballantruan'"..."it has released a peated single malt called Ballantruan". No phenol ppm figure found in the source; general reputation (and the fact it is marketed as Tomintoul's peat-forward counterpart) supports heavy over medium, but the exact figure is not confirmed -- confidence kept low rather than high.

Widely known in general whisky knowledge as a Wemyss Malts blended malt named for its peat character, but every citable source attempted this session (Wemyss's own site, The Whisky Exchange, distiller.com, whisky.com) returned a connection failure or 403. Left peatProfile unknown per the no-citation rule despite the suggestive name -- flagging as a likely "heavy" for reviewer confirmation.
Willett Distillery's best-selling brand (wiki: "Rowan's Creek bourbon (50.05% abv, No age statement) -- This is Willett Distillery's best-selling brand"). Bourbon is not a peated category.

Widely known in general whisky knowledge as a Wemyss Malts blended malt (bourbon-cask/spice-forward, reputed to be unpeated), but no citation could be opened this session confirming this (same access failures as peat-chimney). Left peatProfile unknown per the no-citation rule -- flagging as a likely "none" for reviewer confirmation.

The Kyoto Aka-Obi Red Nishijin-ori -- Nishijin-ori is a real, famous Kyoto textile; Japan is a reasonably confident country guess from the name/theming alone, but no citation confirms the producer, and Japanese blends can legitimately be peated (some Nikka/other blends use peated malt), so peatProfile is left unknown rather than assumed.

Thurso, Caithness -- Scotland's most northerly mainland distillery (authority TSV: Highland/Aurora Brewing). Official site confirms the core range (Northland, Aurora, 10yo, 12yo, Langskip -- the sample product in this batch) is unpeated; Morven is the one peated exception (see rule row). Owner name "Aurora Brewing" as given by the authority TSV; unusual for a distillery but not contradicted elsewhere.

Emitted because ledaig (parentSlug) and alchemist (bottler's sample "Alchemist Tobermory") both need it, per BRIEF.md sec.2. Not itself a brand string in this batch's input, so may also be emitted independently by another batch if "Tobermory" appears as its own catalogue brand there -- harmless duplicate, same facts.

Emitted as old-ballantruan's parentSlug. Wiki: the Tomintoul-branded range (10/12/14/16/21/33yo) carries no peat mention; peat is confined to the separately named Ballantruan/Old Ballantruan and Peaty Tang lines. May also be emitted by another batch if "Tomintoul" is itself a catalogue brand elsewhere -- harmless duplicate.

Emitted as eagle-rare's parentSlug. Frankfort, Kentucky; owned by Sazerac since 1992. Produces both bourbon and rye brands (Eagle Rare, Buffalo Trace, Sazerac rye, etc.) so defaultTypeName left empty. May also be emitted by another batch if "Buffalo Trace" is itself a catalogue brand elsewhere -- harmless duplicate.

Emitted as rowans-creek's parentSlug. Bardstown, Kentucky; family-owned and operated since 1936 (Kulsveen family since the 1980s revival). Produces both bourbon and rye under many labels so defaultTypeName left empty. May also be emitted by another batch if "Willett" is itself a catalogue brand elsewhere -- harmless duplicate.

Emitted as evan-williams's parentSlug. Bardstown/Louisville, Kentucky; largest independent family-owned US spirits producer. Produces bourbon plus other spirits broadly so defaultTypeName left empty. May also be emitted by another batch if "Heaven Hill" is itself a catalogue brand elsewhere -- harmless duplicate.

Emitted as bottlerSlug for peat-chimney and spice-king. Confirmed as a real whisky company via the Kingsbarns distillery wiki page ("owned by Wemyss malts"); peatProfile left unknown as required for a bottler-style range owner.
